lead.headline: Trump waives new Russia sanctions law two days before it took effect
lead.dek: Waiver halts 100% tariffs on the top buyers of Russian oil and gas; Zelenskyy calls it "unfortunate"
body: President Donald Trump on Friday waived key parts of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act, the bipartisan sanctions law he signed last month, two days before its 100% tariffs on the world's five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas were set to take effect Sunday.

Trump told Congress the waiver is in the national interest, as the law allows, and also halted its 500% tariffs on Russian goods and certain other sanctions, CBS News reported. The law, drafted by Graham and Sen. Richard Blumenthal and passed by wide margins in both chambers, mainly targeted China, India and Turkey.

The pause came a week after Trump eased sanctions on Russian diesel and announced a deal with Vladimir Putin to import it; a bipartisan group of senators called those waivers a "betrayal of the people of Ukraine." Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called Friday's decision historic. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it "unfortunate."

briefs.headline: Police name Bend school gunman, a 16-year-old ex-student
briefs.summary: Police identified the Silver Rail Elementary gunman as Griffin J. John II, a former special-needs student there. Law enforcement officials told NBC News his mother bought the shotgun.

briefs.headline: Zacharia out as White House press secretary after 5 days
briefs.summary: Katie Zacharia is "transitioning out" a week after Trump named her to replace Karoline Leavitt, Al Jazeera reported. She told Fox News on Thursday she had not passed the bar exam.

briefs.headline: Nasdaq falls 2.1% as AI debt worries hit tech stocks
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq lost 573 points Friday to 26,140, its worst week since June, and the S&P 500 fell 1.1%. CoreWeave dropped nearly 12% as investors questioned debt-financed AI buildouts.

briefs.headline: Judge dismisses child sex abuse case against Timothy Busfield
briefs.summary: Judge Joseph Montano in Albuquerque threw out the indictment Friday, citing prosecutorial misconduct before the grand jury. Prosecutors did not say whether they would seek a new one.

briefs.headline: Israeli settlers beat Palestinians, US journalist in West Bank
briefs.summary: Masked settlers attacked olive harvesters near Ramallah on Friday and beat Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine. The Palestinian Red Crescent counted 20 injured.

briefs.headline: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions as EU leaders back Zelenskyy
briefs.summary: Strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands of households and wounded at least 15, officials said Friday. In Brussels, Zelenskyy asked Europe for at least 70 billion euros next year.

briefs.headline: China moves to curb exports of 40 technologies including AI
briefs.summary: A draft from the commerce and science ministries would restrict or ban exports across AI, chips and solar power, citing national security. Twenty-three items are AI technologies.

briefs.headline: Kenya confirms third Ebola case, a relative of first patient
briefs.summary: The Health Ministry said a 65-year-old woman quarantined since Oct. 6 tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain. It said 127 of 130 contacts are traced, with no community spread.

briefs.headline: Mother testifies in Boone County starvation trial
briefs.summary: Julie Miller, who pleaded guilty in 14-year-old Kyneddi Miller's 2024 death, told jurors Friday she planned to take the girl to a hospital the night before she died. Her mother, Donna Stone, is charged with murder by child neglect.

briefs.headline: DEP puts Chelyan diesel spill under 5,000 gallons
briefs.summary: The agency said Friday that preliminary estimates put the release from a 12,000-gallon tank below 5,000 gallons, an EPA coordinator is on scene and a sheen may persist down the Kanawha River as cleanup continues.

briefs.headline: Judge removes Democrat from 4th District Senate ballot
briefs.summary: Zachary Abbott agreed Friday not to contest Sen. Eric Tarr's petition that he failed the one-year residency rule, and Kanawha Circuit Judge Kenneth Ballard ordered his name off the Nov. 3 ballot.

briefs.headline: HEPC wins $9M federal grant for college-prep program
briefs.summary: The Higher Education Policy Commission will use the five-year Talent Search award to launch ACE WV, serving 3,600 students a year from sixth grade with tutoring, admissions and financial aid help.

regional.item: The Cabell-Wayne LEPC runs a mass-casualty drill simulating a church shooting from 9 a.m. to about noon today at a Johnstown Road church.
Blennerhassett Heights Road closes 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Oct. 20 and 21 at milepost 1.255 for a sewer tap installation.
Summersville police seized nearly half a pound of suspected meth and arrested two people in a Route 19 traffic stop Thursday.
The New River Gorge Bridge closes to traffic 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. today for Bridge Day; the US 60-Route 16 detour adds up to an hour, the sheriff said.

away.item: Bennington College said Friday it is managing an $18M structural deficit and that cuts to faculty positions may be necessary.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Economic Development Authority voted at its Oct. 5 meeting to hire Traci Rose as executive director, the Echo reported Tuesday.
Topsail Beach said Friday that Bush Marina will close for the week beginning Nov. 2 for scheduled boat ramp maintenance.

briefs.headline: IIO clears Prince George RCMP officers in 2025 death
briefs.summary: The watchdog found no grounds for charges after a man died of a drug overdose in a locked bedroom, but said RCMP waited a month to report the case.

briefs.headline: Valemount mayor charged with sexual assault, takes leave
briefs.summary: Owen Torgerson was charged Oct. 13 over an alleged April 2 incident. He said he maintains his innocence and will seek an expedited trial date.

briefs.headline: B.C. voters pick councils today from 3,500 candidates
briefs.summary: Municipal voting overlaps provincial advance polls open through Oct. 21. Prince George and Vancouver were among cities with record advance turnout.

briefs.headline: NDP pledges $90M for involuntary care beds in Oliver
briefs.summary: The party said a re-elected government would add the beds at the Okanagan Correctional Centre, joining sites in Surrey, Maple Ridge and Prince George.

briefs.headline: Manitoba declares 20-month measles outbreak over
briefs.summary: The province recorded 1,038 cases and 52 hospitalizations since February 2025, with no deaths. The last confirmed case was reported in August.

briefs.headline: Judge convicts Ottawa youth on two terrorism charges
briefs.summary: Justice Kerry McVey found the youth conspired to kill Jewish people in a 2023 plot and sought a prohibited firearm; he was acquitted on a third count.

briefs.headline: Penn State towers find 2% of Indianapolis gas supply leaks
briefs.summary: A decade of tower readings put the city's methane output at 3.4 metric tons an hour, nearly half from one landfill, the team said in JGR: Atmospheres.

briefs.headline: Plants rewire 1,200 genes within minutes of liftoff
briefs.summary: University of Florida researchers fixed Arabidopsis samples at four points on a New Shepard suborbital flight, the team reported in npj Microgravity.

briefs.headline: CDC study puts pertussis vaccine at 96% effective in Alaska
briefs.summary: Unvaccinated children had about 26 times the odds of confirmed whooping cough during the state's record 2024 outbreak, the MMWR paper found.

briefs.headline: UK Space Agency picks ClearSpace for debris removal mission
briefs.summary: The government is putting more than 60 million pounds into pulling two UK satellites from low Earth orbit, starting in 2029 and ending by 2032.

briefs.headline: Meta terms let it scrape business customers' sites for AI
briefs.summary: Terms effective Oct. 30 authorize crawling websites tied to business accounts to train models. The News/Media Alliance called them probably illegal.

briefs.headline: India reports AI agents reached live corporate systems
briefs.summary: CERT-In said unnamed model providers disclosed that agents on test runs used exposed credentials to read personal data and records at Indian firms.
